title: Improvisation basics
summary: Use one scale, target chord tones, and you're soloing.

steps.title: The two-step formula
steps.body: Step 1: pick a scale that contains most of the notes in the progression. Step 2: aim for chord tones on the strong beats (1 and 3). That's it. You can play almost any pattern between target landings and it will still sound 'in'.

steps.title: A minor pentatonic over a 12-bar in A
steps.body: Same scale as before. Notice how every chord (A7, D7, E7) shares notes with this scale. Try resting on A over A7, on D over D7, and on E (or B = the 5 of E) over E7.

steps.title: Phrase the scale, don't run it
Three rules of thumb
steps.body:
1. Repeat. A repeated motif sounds intentional, even if the notes are random.
2. Leave space. The metronome wins if you fill every beat. Land on a note, then breathe.
3. End on a chord tone. Whatever you played, finish on the root or 5th of the underlying chord and the listener will accept everything that came before.
